📚 Scheduling Terms

CP — Critical Path
The longest chain of tasks. If any task on the CP slips, the whole project slips.
TF — Total Float (slack)
Days a task can slip without delaying the project. TF:5d means 5 days breathing room. CP tasks have TF=0.
FF — Free Float
Days a task can slip without delaying the next task.
ES / EF — Early Start / Finish
The soonest a task can start and finish given its predecessors.
LS / LF — Late Start / Finish
The latest a task can start/finish without delaying the project.
◆ Milestone
A point in time, no duration. Like "Foundation poured" or "Handover".
Depends on
Tasks that must finish before this can start. Use task IDs separated by commas: "3, 7, 12".

👋 Welcome to AMELIE·AI

Always Making Every Little Improvement Easy.

AMELIE is a complete project planner for construction, renovation and DIY work. Build a schedule, track materials and labour, watch costs against your budget, and share the result.

The four core ideas:

  • Projects — start blank or pick a template (House Extension, Office Refurb, Kitchen Renovation, etc.)
  • Tasks — what needs doing, with start/due dates and dependencies
  • Timeline — your plan visualised as a Gantt chart with critical path highlighted
  • Resources — Materials, Labour, Hire — all costed against your budget
Your data lives on your device. AMELIE stores everything in your browser's local storage. It never uploads your projects to a server. The only exception is when you explicitly tap an AI button — see the AI section below for what happens then.

🚀 Your first project Beginners

Five steps to a working plan:

1. Tap "+ New project" in the header. Pick a template that's close to your project, or start blank.
2. Open the Tasks tab. Templates come with sensible tasks already loaded. Edit them, add your own with "+ Add task". Set start dates, due dates, and dependencies (which tasks must finish first).
3. Open the Timeline tab. See your plan as a Gantt chart. The red line is today. Red bars are critical-path tasks (the chain that controls when you finish).
4. Add Materials, Labour, Hire as you go. AMELIE auto-totals everything against your budget. Green = under budget, red bold = over budget.
5. Tap 📤 Export when you need to share. Excel, CSV, calendar, PDF — all from one button.

📅 Understanding the Timeline

The Timeline shows every dated task as a horizontal bar. Read it like this:

  • Bar colour tells you status: grey = to do, blue = in progress, green = done, red = overdue, red outline = critical path
  • The red vertical line is today's date — anything to the left is in the past
  • ◆ Diamond shapes are milestones — important dates with no duration (sign-offs, inspections, handover)
  • Arrows between bars show dependencies — "this task must finish before that one starts"
  • CP (Critical Path) in red means: if this task slips, the whole project slips
  • TF (Total Float) is breathing room — TF:5 means the task can slip 5 days without affecting the finish date

Tap any term in the Timeline to see its full definition in the Glossary.

💡 Tips that save your bacon

  • Mark genuinely critical milestones with ◆ — handover, sign-off, inspection dates. These appear as diamonds on the Timeline.
  • Set "Depends on" so the timeline auto-shifts — if Task 5 depends on Task 3, slipping Task 3 automatically pushes Task 5 forward.
  • Tap the ⋮ on any task to insert a new task above or below, move it up/down, or jump it to any position.
  • Voice notes save automatically the moment you stop recording — find them in the Files tab.
  • Photos and files attach to specific tasks — tap the 📎 paperclip on a task row.
  • Use 📥 Backup regularly — your data is local-only, so a backup file is your insurance.

AI AI features (and what happens to your data)

AMELIE includes two AI-powered tools to help you plan smarter. They're optional — everything else works without them.

What the AI can do for you:

  • ⚡ AI Conflict Check — Finds overdue, blocked or undated tasks, broken dependencies, over-budget conditions and un-ordered materials. Detects them on your device, then (optionally) uses the AI to suggest fixes in plain English.
  • AI Review — Reads your project and writes a clean status summary you can send to clients, your boss, or your team.

How it works (the honest version):

When you tap an AI button, AMELIE sends your task data (names, dates, durations, dependencies) to Anthropic — the company that makes Claude, the AI model AMELIE uses. Anthropic processes your request and returns the answer. AMELIE never stores your AI conversations.

What Anthropic does with your data:

  • Anthropic states they do NOT train their AI models on data sent through their API
  • Anthropic retains API data for up to 30 days for safety monitoring, then deletes it
  • You bring your own API key — Anthropic bills you directly, AMELIE never sees the key or your usage

You can read Anthropic's full privacy commitment at anthropic.com/privacy.

Important: AI features are off until you add an Anthropic API key in Settings. If you don't add a key, AMELIE works fully — just without AI suggestions. AMELIE only uses Anthropic — other AI providers may have different privacy policies, and some train their models on your data.
Heads up: Don't paste sensitive data (passwords, bank details, personal client info) into task names or notes if you plan to use AI features. Treat AI input like any other internet service.

📋 Templates & My Templates

AMELIE comes with 12 built-in templates for common projects (House Extension, Office Refurb, Kitchen Renovation, etc.). You can also save your own.

Save your own template:

  • Build a project, get the structure right
  • Open it, go to Overview, tap ⚙ Actions → ⭐ Save as template
  • Pick a name. Dates, progress, photos and files are stripped. Tasks, durations, dependencies, materials, labour and costs are kept.
  • Next time you tap + New project, your saved templates appear at the top under "⭐ My Templates".
Built-in templates are protected — you can use them as starting points, but you can't delete or edit them. Only your personal saved templates can be renamed or deleted (look for ✎ and 🗑 buttons inside the template picker).

🛒 Find suppliers

The 🛒 button in the header opens shortcuts to common builder's merchants — Screwfix, Wickes, Toolstation, B&Q, Home Depot, Hornbach, Leroy Merlin and more. Type what you need (or open it from a material row), pick a supplier, and AMELIE opens that site with your search pre-filled.

Affiliate disclosure: some supplier links are affiliate links. If you buy through them, AMELIE·AI may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. This never changes the price you pay, and it doesn't influence which suppliers are listed — they're chosen to save you typing.

🗑 Delete a project

Two ways to delete a single project:

  • From All Projects view, tap the 🗑 on a project card
  • From inside a project, go to Overview → ⚙ Actions → 🗑 Delete project
Deleting is permanent. AMELIE will ask you to confirm. There's no undo, no rubbish bin, no recovery. If a project matters, use 📤 Export first to save a backup CSV or Excel file.

🔄 Reset the app (start fresh)

If you want to wipe everything and start over — all projects, all templates, all settings:

1. Go to ⚙ Settings in the header
2. Scroll to the Data & Backup section
3. Tap 🗑 Reset / Erase all data and confirm twice

Browser-level reset (if Settings won't open):

  • Open your browser settings → Privacy → Clear browsing data
  • Pick "Cookies and site data" and clear for this site only
  • AMELIE will reload completely fresh next time
Reset cannot be undone. Export anything important first using 📤 Export.

👤 My Profile (your details on prints & exports)

Open 👤 in the header to enter your name, company, role, contact details and an optional company logo. These appear on:

  • Print headers — top of every printed page (visible to anyone you share the print with)
  • 📸 Screenshots — sign-off line under the AMELIE banner
  • Excel and PDF exports — cover sheets and footers carry your name and company
  • Site Diary entries — every entry is signed with your name and timestamp

Logo upload: use a small image under 200KB (PNG with transparent background works best).

Profile data stays on this device only. Nothing is sent anywhere.

📅 Working Calendar (bank holidays & non-working days)

Open 📅 in the header to define when work happens on your project:

  • Region preset — UK, US, EU bank holidays for 2026 and 2027 are pre-loaded. Pick the one closest to your project location.
  • Work weekends? — toggle Mon-Fri vs Mon-Sun.
  • Work bank holidays? — project-level default. Individual tasks can override (e.g. emergency works that run on Christmas Day).
  • Custom non-working days — add specific dates the site won't work: bad weather, planned shutdowns, owner-imposed closures. Each entry is timestamped.

The calendar drives every duration calculation, the critical path, and the Gantt timeline.

Audit log: every change to the calendar (region change, custom day added/removed) is recorded with timestamp and user name. This matters for disruption claims and disputes — contemporaneous records are paramount in construction law.

↩️ Undo & Redo

Made a mistake? Tap ↩️ in the header or press Ctrl+Z to undo the last change. Tap ↪️ or Ctrl+Y to redo. AMELIE keeps up to 10 undo steps per session.

Undo only works for project data changes (tasks, dates, costs, etc). It does not undo profile or calendar changes.

📋 Site Diary & Disruption Register

The 📋 Site Diary tab records site events contemporaneously — the legal standard required by the SCL Delay and Disruption Protocol.

Log weather delays, access issues, variations, stoppages, safety incidents and more. Each entry captures:

  • Date + time · Event type · Headline + full description
  • Hours lost · Trades affected · Manpower impacted · Weather
  • Instruction / variation reference · Witness name(s)
  • Affected tasks (linked from your schedule)

Entries can be edited — but every edit requires a reason and is permanently logged with timestamp and your name. This makes the record MORE credible, not less.

Export a Disruption Register as CSV or print it as a professional PDF report — ready to hand to a QS, solicitor or adjudicator.

Contemporaneous means recorded at the time. Don't reconstruct events days later. Log daily. If a claim ever arises, this record could be the difference between winning and losing.

📋 How AMELIE·AI works (read this first)

AMELIE·AI is a planning tool, not a quotation. It takes your description of intent — what you want to build, dimensions, finishes, zonal areas, fees — and produces an indicative schedule and cost estimate to help you plan and budget.

Quantities and costs are approximations derived from open data sources: UK Government BMCS material indices, ONS construction price indices, FMB labour surveys, and trade-published norms. All under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

The quality of the output depends entirely on the inputs. The more precise your dimensions, zone areas, finish choices, regional setting, VAT rate and adders, the closer the result will be to reality. Vague or incomplete inputs produce vague or incomplete outputs.

Before any purchase or contract commitment, obtain written quotes from suppliers, contractors, and licensed professionals (architect, structural engineer, QS, building control as required). AMELIE·AI's figures are a starting point for conversations, not the conversation itself.

You can refine and override any line: use the ➕ Add custom line button in the header for bespoke items the engine library does not cover. Use the 📈 Rate freshness button to apply the latest UK Government BMCS index figures to your project.

🔤 The ABCs — plain-English glossary

Every term AMELIE uses, in one line each. No jargon left unexplained.

  • Baseline — a saved snapshot of your original plan, so you can compare "where I said I'd be" against "where I actually am."
  • Buffer / Contingency — spare time (or money) you hold back for things that go wrong. AMELIE works out how much you realistically need.
  • Constraint (hard date) — a fixed deadline a task must finish by, e.g. a contract completion date or an NEC4 Key Date.
  • Critical path — the chain of tasks that decides your finish date. Slip one of these and the whole project slips. Shown in red on the Timeline.
  • Criticality index — how often a task lands on the critical path across thousands of simulated runs. A task can be "off" the critical path on paper but critical most of the time in reality — this catches that.
  • Dependency — "this task can't start until that one finishes." The links that make a schedule a schedule rather than a list.
  • DCMA 14-point check — an industry-standard health check for schedules (used by government and big contractors). AMELIE runs it and explains each result in plain English.
  • Float (slack) — how long a task can be delayed before it starts pushing your finish date. Zero float = it's on the critical path.
  • Gantt chart — the Timeline view: each task drawn as a horizontal bar against a calendar.
  • Lead / Lag — a deliberate overlap (lead) or gap (lag) between two linked tasks, e.g. "wait 2 days for plaster to dry before painting" is a lag.
  • Monte Carlo simulation — AMELIE plays out your project thousands of times, each time letting tasks run a bit fast or slow, to show the range of likely finish dates instead of one optimistic guess.
  • Negative float — a warning sign: a task is already projected to miss its deadline before you've even started. AMELIE flags it red.
  • P50 / P80 / P95 — confidence levels. P80 = "80% likely you'll finish by this date." Most professionals commit to a P80 date, not the best-case plan date.
  • S-curve — the graph that climbs from "best case" to "almost certain." You pick your confidence level and read across to the date.
  • Sensitivity / Tornado chart — ranks which tasks' uncertainty drives your finish date the most, so you know where to focus. Longest bar = biggest risk lever.
  • Three-point estimate — instead of one duration, you give an optimistic, most-likely, and pessimistic number. This is what feeds the risk analysis.
  • WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) — grouping tasks into phases or areas, like chapters in a book.
New to all this? You don't need most of it to start. Build a few tasks, set dates, and explore. The risk terms (P80, tornado, Monte Carlo) only matter once you want a finish date you can defend to a client. The guided tour (top of this Help screen) walks you through the lot on a practice project.
